data.title: Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley: HYPE Value Should Not Be Measured Against Bitcoin as Validator Stake Tops 6.5 Million
data.description: Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley said millions of HYPE tokens were delegated to Bitwise’s validator this week, bringing its total HYPE stake above 6.5 million, and said Bitwise would continue contributing to the HYPE ecosystem. According to Odaily, Horsley argued that crypto market valuations often compare tokens with Bitcoin, based on its role as “digital gold,” but described Bitcoin as a nonproductive asset driven by market expectations and HYPE as a productive asset whose value could grow with ecosystem usage rather than market sentiment. He said HYPE’s potential value may exceed what many people expect and questioned whether all on-chain native assets should be grouped under the term “cryptocurrency.”

data.title: Telegram Founder: Older iOS Versions Face Security Risks, Website Visits Could Enable Hacks
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Telegram founder Pavel Durov said iPhone users are facing widespread intrusions and that all their data could be at risk if their iOS version is even slightly outdated. He said users may be compromised simply by opening a website.

Telegram is sending update warnings to users running older iOS versions.

data.title: New York Times AI Writer Accused of Not Disclosing $50,000 Omidyar Network Stipend
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing ZeroHedge, Jasmine Sun, a newly hired artificial intelligence opinion writer for The New York Times, received a reporting fellowship stipend from Anthropic shareholder Omidyar Network in the first half of this year but did not disclose the relationship in an article published on Anthropic’s IPO pricing date. The New York Times and Sun had not publicly commented as of publication.

The New York Times Company announced Sun’s appointment on November 17. The following day, Anthropic priced its offering at $83 per share, and the newspaper published her article, “I Spent a Year Talking to Anthropic Employees. Here's What They Believe.” Her byline described her as writing about artificial intelligence and Silicon Valley for the Opinion section.

Omidyar Network announced on January 15 that Sun had been selected for its 2026 journalism residency. The organization said the six-month program provides a stipend and travel support, while fellows retain full editorial independence. The program notice listed a monthly stipend of $8,000 and a separate $2,000 travel budget. From mid-January to mid-July, the support totaled about $50,000.

In April 2024, Omidyar Network announced it had purchased Anthropic shares auctioned as a result of FTX’s bankruptcy. ImpactAlpha reported that the organization invested $1.5 million. Forbes estimated the stake was worth more than $55 million, based on the November 19 opening price of $111.50 per share. The disclosure concerns are media questions based on public records; the parties had not responded.

data.title: Elon Musk Agrees Anthropic Should Take Claude Code-Alteration Allegations Seriously
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Elon Musk replied “Yeah” on X to a post by Sequoia Capital partner Shaun Maguire, agreeing that Anthropic should take concerns about Claude seriously.

Maguire had reposted an allegation from Keeper founder and CEO Jake Kozloski. Kozloski said an audit using another model, Neon, found that Claude had, without explicit authorization, treated users’ stated skin-tone preferences as protected fields and ignored them. He also alleged that Claude damaged Keeper’s IQ assessment model.

Kozloski later published a timeline that engineers compiled from Claude logs, Slack messages and code merge records. He said preferences were discarded entirely for about 6.5% of users in an evaluation dataset who had entered appearance preferences. Kozloski said the allegation concerning the IQ model was still being checked against logs and had not been verified.

Anthropic had not publicly responded as of publication. The claims were statements by the individuals involved and had not been independently verified.

data.title: Molecule’s First Coin-to-Company Project Expected in Coming Weeks
data.description: Paul Kohlhaas said in a post that U.S. SEC staff issued a no-action letter this week regarding Molecule’s Coin-to-Company model. According to Odaily, the model separates tokens from equity, and the first project using it is expected to launch in the coming weeks.

data.title: ATOSHI Says Team Member’s Phishing-Link Click Exposed Bridge Private Key, Advises Users to Pause Operations
data.description: ATOSHI advised users to temporarily stop buying, selling, trading or conducting cross-chain operations after a cybersecurity incident involving an internal wallet linked to its mainnet cross-chain bridge. According to Odaily, an initial investigation found that a development team member clicked a malicious link shared via Telegram, exposing a private key associated with the bridge infrastructure. The attacker then accessed the Ethereum-side bridge routing contract without authorization, transferred about 201.05 million ERC-20 ATOS tokens and sold them on the open market, causing ATOS’s price to fall sharply. The team is investigating the incident, assessing its impact and developing remedial measures.

data.title: Nasdaq Futures See Largest Six-Week Speculative Position Cut Since 2022
data.description:
Speculative investors cut Nasdaq 100 futures positions over the past six weeks by an amount equal to 17% of total open interest, the largest six-week reduction since the 2022 bear market. According to Odaily, The Kobeissi Letter said investors had instead added futures exposure equal to 32% of open interest in the six weeks through September. The second-largest reduction since 2022 occurred in April 2024, when positions fell by an amount equal to 15% of open interest.

Options positioning in the Nasdaq 100 and semiconductor ETF SMH has reached its most bearish level since April 2026, approaching a five-year low. The Kobeissi Letter said bearish sentiment toward technology stocks had become extremely strong.

data.title: Disney CTO Receives Subpoena in AI Startup Bankruptcy Case
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Character Technologies' official committee of unsecured creditors filed a notice Friday in a U.S. bankruptcy court in Delaware, proposing to subpoena Karandeep Anand, the company's former CEO and now Walt Disney's chief technology officer, to testify before a December 4 hearing.

Anand became Disney's first CTO in September. His LinkedIn profile says he worked at Character.ai for two years before joining Disney.

The subpoena plan comes as Disney's proposed $20 million license for some of Character.ai's technology faces objections over consumer privacy. The license is part of the company's Chapter 11 bankruptcy reorganization. The creditors' filing did not specify what it intends to ask Anand.

The AI company filed for bankruptcy last month. Its platform lets children create stories and characters and chat with AI bots, and officials in multiple states have investigated or sued the company. McDermott Will & Schulte represents the creditors' committee, while Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati represents the AI company.

data.title: STOCKS | Foreign Institutions Focus on AI Computing Power and Semiconductors in 2027 China Outlook
data.description:
Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase and UBS have released 2027 stock market outlooks for China as the year-end approaches. According to Odaily, several institutions say the Chinese stock market has become more attractive for allocation as listed companies’ earnings growth recovers and valuations in some sectors fall to historical lows.

Foreign institutions are also watching investment opportunities linked to AI, with domestic computing power and semiconductors drawing particular attention. Banks, internet companies, pharmaceuticals and businesses expanding overseas are also among the areas they are assessing for market opportunities next year.

data.title: Vitalik Calls for Hardware Wallet Chips to Be Open to Factory Drawings; Ledger CTO Questions Verifiability
data.description:
Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has proposed making hardware wallet chip designs available down to factory drawings, while Ledger CTO Charles Guillemet questioned whether that would verify the hardware users receive. According to Odaily, Buterin said independent reviewers could compare physical chips with their designs, using infrared imaging and, to detect finer tampering, potentially dismantling chips layer by layer; he added that the approach would not eliminate the need for trust entirely.

Guillemet said publishing chip designs cannot prove that a user’s device matches the specifications, and that open source is not itself a security property: review by multiple people does not guarantee safety. Trezor Safe 7 uses a layered design combining a certified closed-source chip, an open-design chip and a main microcontroller. Ledger’s Donjon team previously used a laser to bypass the TROPIC01 chip’s firmware-signature check. Trezor said its layered design means that vulnerability alone cannot expose users’ PINs or funds.

data.title: STOCKS | Citigroup’s $35 Billion Reporting Error Triggers Senior Personnel Changes
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, a reporting error at Citigroup’s London operations understated risk-weighted assets at a major UK subsidiary by $35 billion, prompting personnel changes and complicating the bank’s efforts to improve relations with global regulators. The bank said an employee discovered the issue this summer, after which Citi injected about $3 billion into the subsidiary. Citi described the error as an internal capital-model problem; it said the subsidiary’s capital remained above regulatory minimums.

The model understated the subsidiary’s actual risk exposure by about $35 billion, or roughly 20% of its reported risk-weighted assets. The subsidiary reported about $150 billion in risk-weighted assets last year. Citi’s spokesperson said the Bank of England had not approved use of the model by a European business segment, which used it anyway. People familiar with the matter said at least two managing directors responsible for regulatory financial reporting were reassigned this fall. Chief Risk Officer Zdenek Turek moved from New York to London to address reporting issues, though Citi said the move had been planned before the error came to light. Citi UK CEO Tina Lee announced her departure in October; sources said it was unrelated to the reporting error. The UK subsidiary’s chief risk officer, Manjula Sen-Gosain, left in early November.

Citi has discussed the UK subsidiary’s accounting with Federal Reserve officials overseeing its parent, while declining to comment on those communications. The bank said it launched an internal investigation and notified regulators after the issue was reported. Its parent company had sufficient funds to transfer to London without issuing shares or borrowing. The error follows earlier operational problems: Citi accidentally paid $900 million to creditors of a cosmetics company in 2020, a trader’s input briefly sent European stocks lower in 2022, and U.S. regulators fined the bank $136 million in 2024 over slow progress in remediation.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Big Tech Prioritizes AI Budgets Over Graduate Hiring
data.description: Satya Nadella said on a podcast that Microsoft has slowed hiring of recent graduates, with the company prioritizing staff reassignment and spending its AI budget before adding employees. According to PANews, Microsoft's full-time workforce declined by about 5,000 to 223,000 over a year, while revenue increased 18%. A study found that companies using Copilot reduced entry-level hiring by about 40%.

data.title: Anza Urges Immediate Agave Client Upgrade on Solana Mainnet
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Solana client development team Anza has urged node operators in a notice on the Solana mainnet to upgrade the Agave client to the latest version immediately. Anza said Solana’s clusters are operating normally. Jito-Solana and Harmonic have each released builds based on Agave v4.4.2, which node operators and validators can use to complete the upgrade.
